references.text: Moses' earlier mention of the same forty days and forty nights when he threw himself down before the Lord because of the people's sin with the golden calf
Moses summarizes that he was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights, and the Lord heard his prayer and did not want to destroy the people
The parallel account in Exodus where the Lord says He will destroy the people, and Moses intercedes for them
Moses was with the Lord for forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water
Another occasion where the Lord threatened to destroy the people because of their disobedience
The context of Moses' fast on the mountain, forty days and forty nights without bread and water
The psalmist's reference to how Moses stood in the breach for the people to prevent God's wrath from destroying them
